\chapter{Introduction}
\label{ch:introduction}

Students who write a thesis together rarely sit in the same room. They edit
the same files from different machines, often at the same time, and expect
every change to show up for everyone within a second. Systems that do this
well build on ideas from distributed systems \cite{lamport78} and from
replicated data types \cite{shapiro11}.

\section{Problem statement}
A server that relays edits must remember the current state of each document.
Reading that state from disk on every connection is slow; keeping all of it
in memory does not scale. Chapter~\ref{ch:background} reviews the options and
Chapter~\ref{ch:evaluation} measures them.

\section{Contributions}
\begin{itemize}
  \item A model of the read and write load of a small editing group.
  \item Measurements of three caching strategies on that load.
  \item A recommendation for servers with fewer than fifty users.
\end{itemize}
